messages:
tayla: Opening a docs PR for IPSec/strongSwan guidance for Private deployments to reach on-prem KMS/HSM. Goal: provide an alternative to WireGuard for customers behind strict corporate firewalls. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/YYYY. Need network and security review.

devops: Nice. Key asks: show connlimit/DPD settings, esp for HSM admin consoles that drop idle connections. Also include NAT-T/ESP fallback notes and how to enable opportunistic UDP encapsulation.

aaron: Agree. Please include an IKEv2 cert-based example (client cert from our CA) and a PSK fallback example. Many enterprise customers will insist on certs.

rachel: Add a short section on path MTU / DF handling with ESP headers. Recommend lowering MTU on tunnel to 1396 for ethernet(1500) to account for ESP overhead, and include how to test with iperf3 -M or ping -s.

doc-ally: Can we surface a minimal iptables and nftables example for the most common layouts? Also include the minimal systemd/unit file and how to ship certs in an offline bundle for air-gapped installs (example dir /etc/redwood/kms-ipsec/).

tayla: Draft snippets I'm planning to include below. Please point out any vendor/HSM caveats.

```
# /etc/ipsec.conf (simplified)
config setup
    uniqueids=no
    charondebug=\"ike 1, knl 1, cfg 0\"

conn redwood-kms
    left=%any
    leftid=@redwood-private
    leftcert=/etc/redwood/kms-ipsec/client.p12
    leftsendcert=always
    leftfirewall=yes
    leftsubnet=10.10.0.0/24
    right=kms.example.com
    rightid=@kms-host
    rightsubnet=10.20.0.0/24
    auto=add
    ike=aes256-sha256-modp2048!
    esp=aes256gcm16-modp2048
    dpdaction=restart
    dpddelay=30s
    rekey=no
    fragmentation=yes
    encapsulation=yes # enable NAT-T if behind NAT
```

# quick cert-based ipsec secret example (in /etc/ipsec.secrets)
: P12 \"/etc/redwood/kms-ipsec/client.p12\" \"client-password\"
```

rachel: For fragmentation, also add a note to disable TCP MSS clamping on the HSM side if the HSM vendor docs require passthrough. Some vendors recommend leaving MSS alone and adjusting MTU instead.

devops: Add test commands everyone can run: `ip xfrm state`, `ip xfrm policy`, `sudo journalctl -u strongswan -f`, `swanctl --list-sas`. For connectivity tests: `curl --interface <tunnel-ip> https://kms.example.com:7443/healthz`

aaron: For air-gapped packaging: show a manifest example that includes client.p12, vendor root CA, and a SHA256 checksum file. Example dir: `/opt/offline-bundle/redwood/kms-ipsec/` and a post-install script that imports the p12 into /etc/ipsec.d/ and sets file perms 640 root:root.

doc-ally: Good. Also include a short migration checklist from Dedicated->Private: stage tunnel in parallel, verify admin-plane reachability to HSM (TCP 7443 or vendor port), schedule maintenance window for final cutover.

rachel: Quick security note: for HSMs that expose management interfaces, recommend applying source-IP allowlists at the HSM side and using a bastion if vendor doesn't support src filtering. Call this out clearly.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/YYYY (files: docs/private/ipsec-strongswan-kms.md, examples/ipsec-manifest.md, snippets/ipsec-tests.md)

devops: One more ask: include an example of how to enable and pin kernel crypto modules on older kernels (`modprobe af_key; modprobe esp4`) and a troubleshooting tip for 'no suitable algorithm' errors in strongSwan logs.

aaron: Suggest adding a tiny troubleshooting table: symptom / likely cause / quick check -- e.g., 'IKE SA not established' -> missing cert trust / check `swanctl --list-certs` and `openssl pkcs12 -info -in client.p12`.

tayla: Thanks everyone. I'll incorporate these and add a small vendor caveats section with a reminder to check HSM vendor docs on allowed management ports. Will ping when ready for final review.
